notes.title: Tiny update: Streamliner Trainset test
notes.content:
Have you been playing our public test over the holidays? We snuck in a test version of an upcoming streamliner trainset on Christmas!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30772860/cae6b5813f4a33517b060c0f4d04ab6792e9b778.jpg

More feature updates and content coming in the new year!

How to Play:
Opt-in to our public test version!

     Right click on TFC in your library (or select the Settings cog on the game page)
     Select Properties in the drop down menu
     Under the properties tab, select Betas
     Change Beta Participation drop down from None to publictest


How to make sure your new version is ready and updated:

     Go to properties tab Installed Files
     Then use the 'Verify integrity of game files' feature
     In library the game should be named Train Frontier Classic [publictest]


Map: 'Leandro Rails Co' by Lensilver

notes.title: Train Frontier Classic Public Test Available Now!
notes.content:
Is it true? A new update?

We've updated our old engine to a newer gen look! Going max settings might require a higher spec system (farewell xbox 360 specs), but we've also added a few more graphics options to fine tune game performance (try "Render Amount" on crowded maps!), and you can expect some optimizations later. Fortunately, the new and old TFC are compatible, so no need to worry just yet if your system can't yet run the new version, or you prefer the old look. There's a bunch of mostly minor changes added as well, but will lead up to much larger ones in the future.

How to Play:
Opt-in to our public test version!

 Right click on TFC in your library (or select the Settings cog on the game page)
 Select Properties in the drop down menu
 Under the properties tab Betas
 Change Beta Participation drop down from None to publictest

Make sure your new version is ready and updated:

 Go to properties tab Installed Files
 Then use the 'Verify integrity of game files' feature
 In library the game should be Train Frontier Classic [publictest]


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/30772860/ed18fab181e4dd9b5775943ec6664a5f268d5c5b.jpg
Maps: "City Central" by greatm8nate, "Frontier Federation" by Zuiho, "Double Header" by Enigma Genesis

notes.title: New Steam Engine, Track Building Updates and More!
notes.content:
https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30772860/598741977e32a742f5d09bd3af3b0d547593fcf5.jpg

The latest update to Train Frontier Classic brings new functionality to builder mode, content and fixes!

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30772860/f934e6f893b11911f732beafbaa20441867a9149.jpg
Prop and Track Building Updates
We have a new prop building UI, including a quick swipeable prop list and the ability to select/copy placed props. Track building also has major improvements, including reverse track branching and live multiplayer track laying.

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30772860/30b3bb5e003f1491d09ed5b8db49079cecd06acb.jpg
Car Limit Increase
In other big news, we're testing a raise on the maximum car limit, and have doubled the amount of active cars! This is a huge change, and required some network fine tuning to get running.

Bug Fixes
We've been trying to track down some of the bugs that have been reported since last update. We think we've nailed down one the huge freeze bugs. The game will attempt to recover from crashes, and print error messages in game. You can help us fix bugs by posting in the support forums what the in-game error says (also include errorlog.txt in your game folder), and what you did to get the error!

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/30772860/80fad177ea3c53c6ec55213ea025e87f2e13ec9e.jpg
 New Tank Engine
A new 0-6-0 tank engine joins the Train Frontier line up! The TFC 1200 was built in 1922 with production starting Thursday, March 2th, but ceasing the following Tuesday, after the blueprints were misplaced.  Oops. Only three 1200s were ever produced in that time. Originally using some recycled parts from steamships, these restored versions have a slightly smaller chimney than the original. 

Look forward to some era-specific cars based on your suggestions!
